text:
jin: heads up — az3 started a big eviction wave at ~01:03 UTC, ~45 tiny-gang pods evicted in 20m window
oncall-bot: :warning: ALERT: eviction-spike detected in cluster/az3 (45 evictions) — auto-created incident #INC-7421
sam: wow that's large for tiny jobs, any pattern on node types?
jin: mostly mixed GPU nodes (A100+T4) that we packed last month for utilization. Many pods had nodeAffinity to 'gpu:small' which matched T4s but anti-affinity requested packing which fragmented slots.
linda: can you paste the scheduler logs for a failed schedule?
jin: sure, here's a short excerpt from kube-scheduler logs around a failure:
```
I0320 01:03:12.345678 1 factory.go:199] Prioritizing nodes for pod tiny-job-234
I0320 01:03:12.346001 1 predicate.go:87] Pod requires gpu:small affinity -> matched nodes: 12
I0320 01:03:12.346400 1 score.go:45] TopologySpreadScore applied -> node scores cluster wide -> prefers spreading
I0320 01:03:12.346900 1 schedule_error.go:52] Fit failed: Insufficient resources: requested=1 GPU, available=0 in selected shape
```
matt: ah the topology spread + our new rack-level taint policy causes the scheduler to prefer scattering, leaving 1-GPU gaps on A100 nodes. tiny jobs end up on T4s but then get preempted when a larger job lands.
sam: any quick mitigation we can do? revert topologySpread weight?
jin: short-term: revert the topology weight change we rolled last Friday (it pushed for spread on pods with label role=tiny). Also launch a descheduler job to consolidate tiny pods onto T4-only nodepools and cordon a handful of mixed nodes so big jobs land on A100 islands.
linda: does descheduler have a safe compacting policy? I don't want mass restarts during peak traffic.
matt: use descheduler's RemoveDuplicates + LowNodeUtilization with a conservative threshold (0.25 -> 0.4), run in dry-run for 10m then real. Also we can tag nodes with node.kubernetes.io/compact-prefer=true and run a small controller to prefer packing there.
jin: plan I propose:
- 01:35 UTC: revert topology weight change (configmap) -> rollout to kube-scheduler canary in az3 only
- 01:45 UTC: enable descheduler dry-run for tiny pod label, collect impact metrics (evictions, restart counts)
- 02:15 UTC: cordon 6 mixed-gpu nodes (old packing suspects) and drain non-critical tiny pods to compact pools
- 03:00 UTC: uncordon and re-evaluate, follow up with a scheduled defrag job overnight
sam: sounds reasonable. What's the cost impact if we keep current behavior another day?
jin: estimate: 45 evictions -> avg pod restart 120s impact + 2x more scheduling overhead. Extra GPU-hours due to inefficient packing ~ 8 GPU-hours expensive instance (~$12/hr equivalents) -> ~ $100/day if sustained. Also customer tail latency increases.
linda: ok set the descheduler dry-run and alert config. I can own the canary rollback if the scheduler change causes regressions.
jin: assigning myself to the revert and descheduler rollout. matt will handle cordon/drain runbooks. sam please prep a quick metric dashboard (eviction rate, pod restarts, avg pod packing density) and pin to #eng-platform
matt: got it. I'll add a safety gate script to pause drains if eviction/restart rate spikes beyond expected.
oncall-bot: Incident INC-7421 updated: mitigation actions started (revert topology config + descheduler dry-run).
jin: thank you — will post updates every 15m. If anyone sees unexpected mass restarts drop a note here. :thumbsup:
